cards.explanation: The answer is True. Joshua, Israel's leader, says it plainly: “All this time you have not deserted your brothers, up to this very day, but have kept the charge given you by the LORD your God.” That's a long stretch of showing up, friends. Most of us can't keep a plant alive that long, and these three tribes kept their word.

The answer is to love the LORD and hold fast to Him. Joshua sends these tribes home with one big assignment, and it isn't about the land or the loot. Moses the servant of the LORD gave them the call “to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to hold fast to Him…” Hold fast, like somebody gripping a hot tray and NOT letting go. Love first, and holding on tight right behind it.

The word is divide. Joshua says, “Divide with your brothers the spoil of your enemies.” These tribes are going home rich, and he tells them to share it. Think of it like baking a big batch of cookies and not eating the whole tray alone. Okay, I've been tempted.

The answer is altar, friends. The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh build an imposing one at Geliloth, right by the Jordan. Imposing is the text's own word for it. Keep an eye on that altar, because it's about to cause a stir.

The answer is False. The report says the altar is “…on the border of the land of Canaan, at Geliloth near the Jordan on the Israelite side.” So it isn't out in Gilead on the far side. It's on the Canaan side of the river. The details of where it sits are part of the report Israel hears.

The answer is war, friends. When they heard the report, the whole congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh to go to war against the three tribes. That's a big jump from hearing about one altar. I think they were very worried about what it meant.

The answer is one family leader from each tribe. Ten chiefs go, “…one family leader from each tribe of Israel, each the head of a family among the clans of Israel.” And Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, walks right alongside them. When ten family heads show up at your door together, nobody's asking if you want to talk. They're telling you it's time to talk.

The answer is turning away from the LORD. That's how the delegation puts it. They ask, “What is this breach of faith you have committed today against the God of Israel by turning away from the LORD and building for yourselves an altar…” A little later they ask, “And now, would you turn away from the LORD?” That's a serious charge to bring to their own brothers.

The answer is False. The leaders warn, “If you rebel today against the LORD, tomorrow He will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.” The whole congregation, not just three tribes. That's why they didn't just shrug and go home.

The answer is to cross over and settle among them. The leaders say, “If indeed the land of your inheritance is unclean, then cross over to the land of the LORD’s possession, where the LORD’s tabernacle stands, and take possession of it among us.” They're ready to make room for their brothers. Not a bad offer from people who showed up ready for a fight.

The answer is False. The leaders remind everyone that Achan, son of Zerah, was unfaithful regarding what was set apart for destruction, bringing wrath on the whole congregation. Then they add, “Yet it was not only Achan who perished because of his sin!” His sin cost others too.

The word is spare. The tribes say, “If this was in rebellion or breach of faith against the LORD, do not spare us today.” Think about that, friends. They're saying that if they're guilty, go ahead and don't go easy on them. That's a bold way to start a defense.

The answer is “You have no share in the LORD.” That's their fear. They say future descendants might tell theirs, “For the LORD has made the Jordan a border between us and you Reubenites and Gadites. You have no share in the LORD!” So the river itself was part of the worry. I think it would sting to hear that, friends.

The word is witness, friends. They say, “…let it be a witness between us and you and the generations to come, that we will worship the LORD in His presence…” It's meant to keep speaking long after everyone in this conversation is gone. A bit like a photo on the fridge, telling the story to whoever walks by.

The answer is a replica of the LORD's altar. They say they would answer, “Look at the replica of the altar of the LORD that our fathers made, not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you.” So it's a copy and not a rival. Pointing at something people can see beats a long speech any day.

The answer is False, friends. They say, “Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away from Him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices, other than the altar of the LORD our God, which stands before His tabernacle.” Their offerings belong on the LORD's altar. The one they built is a witness and not a second place to sacrifice.

The answer is True. The text says that when Phinehas the priest and the chiefs heard what the descendants of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh had to say, “…they were satisfied.” They had come with a hard question, and the answer they got was enough for them. I bet those chiefs felt a lot lighter on the walk back.

The answer is the hand of the LORD. Phinehas tells them, “Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this breach of faith against Him. Consequently, you have delivered the Israelites from the hand of the LORD.” It's a big thing to say to people you showed up ready to argue with. Honest, too.

The answer is that Israel blesses God and drops the war. The text says, “The Israelites were satisfied with the report, and they blessed God and spoke no more about going to war against them…” They went from gathering for war to blessing God. The whole mood flipped.
